backgrounds.local: You pulled the Ruddock boy out of the millrace the spring the water came up. Wickmoor has not let you forget it, and would not let you if you asked.
Cotter's apprentice, three years at the anvil. Your early work still hangs on the far wall, crooked, and he has never once taken it down.
Ilsa Rooke taught you your letters out of the Accord's book, and a good deal she was not supposed to teach anyone.
You came up the North Road on your own at nine and nobody ever quite established from where. Halla fed you anyway.
Small things, mostly. Tollgate scrip that was never issued, a lamp-tithe ledger with a page that does not add up. Nobody has proved it.
Your people worked the high wood before the Syndicate priced the pitch. You know the ground past the treeline better than the road.
Too young for the war, old enough for the levy that came after it. Six months holding a line that was never attacked, and it marked you anyway.
You read. In Wickmoor that is nearly a disease, and Sibby has been lending you things she should not.
